model: Lender FCFE at cost of equity on cash EBTDA less book-growth equity (engine route)

inputs.share_count_basis: 1,245.9m ordinary shares on issue at 30-Jun-2026 (FY26 AR line 91) + 13.6m dilutive options/rights (FY26 AR note EPS B). Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows and Zip settles awards by on-market purchase (A$24.6m FY26) and buys back stock (A$120.9m FY26). Warrants excluded as non-dilutive per the filing.
inputs.sbc_source: FY26 Annual Report cash-EBTDA reconciliation, share-based payments A$19.8m (line 3166); no net-share-settlement tax line (awards settled by A$24.6m on-market purchase, which is the cash form of the same cost)
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity, not WACC: the flow is post-funding-cost equity cash, so it is discounted at CoE. AUD 10y govt ~4.4% + beta ~1.5 x 6.0% AUD ERP = ~13.4%, rounded to 13.0% because the bear scenario carries the credit-cycle risk explicitly (risk charged once, same rate every scenario).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment in flows: lease cash (~A$5m/yr, liabilities A$9.4m) charged via lease_cost_pct_path because cash EBTDA is pre-IFRS16-depreciation; no lease liability in the bridge.
inputs.last_fcf_note: last_fcf is a FY26 FCFE proxy, NOT reported_fcf - sbc - interest_income: cash EBTDA 268.9 - SBC 19.8 - cash tax 20.3 - capex 23.0 - lease ~5 - equity share (~10%) of the A$359m gross receivables increase ~36 = ~145. Reported OCF-less-capex (-108.9) is dominated by receivables-book funding and is not a free cash flow for a lender.
inputs.notes: MODEL: routed as a specialty consumer lender (BNPL), not an operating company. Zip funds a ~A$3.0bn receivables book with ~A$2.75bn of securitised warehouse/ABS borrowings; that debt is operating funding (its interest sits above cash EBTDA as a cost of sales), so like a bank's deposits it is NOT net debt: net_debt=0 and the flow is FCFE at cost of equity (same engine convention as NAB.AX/CHC.AX). Engine mapping: revenue = total income; 'EBITDA' = Group Cash EBTDA (after funding costs and net bad debts, before provision movement, SBC and D&A); SBC deducted explicitly; D&A for tax only; capex = PP&E + capitalised software/intangibles; working-capital capture NEGATIVE = equity Zip must retain to fund receivables growth (receivables/total income ~2.24x, ~8-11% of the book equity-funded via seller notes/first-loss and restricted cash => ~20% of each $ of revenue growth). Mid-cycle discipline: history FY21-FY23 is loss-making (FY22 A$821m impairment on failed UK/EU/Twisto/Spotii; FY23 A$41m discontinued loss), FY24 NI includes a A$139.7m convertible-note extinguishment gain and FY25 a A$54.6m DTA recognition, so no growth rate is extrapolated from statutory NI or OCF; the base path is anchored to FY27 guidance (cash EBTDA A$340m, operating margin 20-22%) and then decays. NZ wind-down (Jul-26) is small (<5% of income) and treated as immaterial. Cash tax: FY26 paid A$20.3m; tax losses largely consumed (A$98.7m left, unrecognised), so rate ramps up; path is expressed on the engine's EBIT (which is before the ~3.5%-of-revenue provision build and funding-cost amortisation), hence ~22% on engine EBIT ~ 27% blended AU30/US~25% on true PBT. Buybacks A$29.1m FY25 / A$120.9m FY26 (A$150m program complete) are a use of the FCFE the model already counts; value-neutral here. Possible Nasdaq dual listing is not modelled (no cash-flow effect; re-rating only).
inputs.sanity_note: Year-1 base: revenue ~A$1,617m, cash EBTDA ~A$340m (ties to guidance), FCFE ~A$175m => ~7% yield on ~A$2.5bn market cap.

equity_bridge.note: FY26 AR Available Cash and Liquidity A$246.5m (after restricted cash A$224.8m and operational floats A$28.3m). ~A$146m retained as operating buffer/book-growth equity; A$100m treated as distributable surplus (management flags further capital management in FY27). Interest earned on it (~A$4m) remains in total income -- immaterial overlap (~A$0.02/share).

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is meaningless as a growth anchor: 5yr (-9.7%) reflects the FY22 A$821m impairment and FY21-23 losses; 3yr (+42.2%) reflects the FY24 recapitalisation/equity raise and convertible extinguishment gain. EPS and FCF CAGRs are undefined (negative bases; OCF swings with receivables funding). Revenue CAGR is backward-looking; the forward base path starts at ~20% (FY27 guidance) and decays.
historical_growth.notes: FY26 total income +24.6%, cash EBTDA +57.9%, statutory NPAT A$116.4m. Owner-FCF (OCF basis) is not a meaningful series for a lender and is not used for CAGRs.

base.wc_capture_rationale: Negative: equity funding of receivables growth (~2.2x revenue book, ~9% equity-funded).

scenario_narratives.base: FY27 lands on guidance (cash EBTDA ~A$340m, 21% operating margin) as US TTV grows ~30% in USD, then growth decays toward nominal GDP by FY36 as the US book matures and Pay-in-2/Stripe/Google distribution is absorbed. Group margin drifts to 23% (US already 25%, ANZ 16% improving; NZ exit removes a sub-scale drag). US net bad debts stay inside the 1.5-2.0% of TTV band and warehouse funding margins hold. Zip retains ~20c of equity per $1 of revenue growth to fund the book and returns the rest via buybacks.
scenario_narratives.bull: US embedded-finance distribution (Stripe GA, Google Pay, Visa, agentic commerce) keeps US TTV growth >30% for two more years and above 15% into FY30; scale lowers funding costs further (Nasdaq listing broadens the investor and ABS base) and operating margin climbs to 26% as fixed tech/opex is leveraged. Credit stays benign. Exit at 12x FCFE reflects a re-rating toward US BNPL peers.
scenario_narratives.bear: A US consumer-credit downturn hits Zip's low-to-middle-income, credit-constrained customer base in FY28: net bad debts break above 2% of TTV, warehouse spreads widen at renewal, management shrinks originations and margin falls to ~13% before recovering only to 17% as Afterpay/Klarna/Affirm and bank-native instalment products compress merchant take rates and the AU NCCP regime lifts compliance cost. Growth settles at 3-6%. Exit at 8x reflects a structurally lower-quality lender.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 30% (above the 15% default): unsecured lending to non-prime consumers late in a credit cycle, dependence on warehouse renewals, and a history of value-destructive expansion. Base 50%: FY26 beat and FY27 guidance give a credible near-term anchor. Bull 20% (below the 35% default): requires sustained >30% US growth, margin expansion and benign credit simultaneously.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Zip is valued as a specialty lender: equity free cash flow (cash EBTDA after SBC, cash tax, capex, leases and the equity it must retain to fund receivables growth) discounted at a 13% AUD cost of equity, with warehouse/ABS debt treated as operating funding rather than net debt. Statutory history is too distorted by impairments (FY22), discontinued losses (FY23), a convertible extinguishment gain (FY24) and a DTA recognition (FY25) to extrapolate; the projection is anchored to FY27 guidance and decays to mid-cycle margins, with a heavier bear weight for credit-cycle risk.
key_risks_to_valuation: Credit losses on a non-prime US book in a downturn (bear case margin trough ~13%)
Warehouse funding cost/renewal risk; ABS spreads widen in stress
Take-rate compression from Afterpay/Block, Klarna, Affirm, PayPal and bank instalment products
Equity-funding share of the book (wc_capture) is estimated, not disclosed; each 5pp moves base IV ~A$0.10-0.15/share
AUD/USD: ~59% of income is USD; a stronger AUD cuts reported cash EBTDA
Capital-allocation risk (history of failed M&A; possible Nasdaq listing)

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 1.375-4.93
